verdicts.tldr: the RangeStmt rule's `n.Op != DEFINE` wrapper is residue of the old shape: isCrossingCurParam already answers false for every range DEFINE, 13 lines fold to 7
verdicts.details: isCrossingCurParam switches on last.GetBlockNodeForPath(store, nx.Path) and returns true only for *FuncDecl and *FuncLitExpr (preprocess.go:6115-6121). A range DEFINE binds its key and value into the RangeStmt's own block at TRANS_BLOCK (`last.Define(kn, anyValue(kt))`, preprocess.go:3049-3086) and the block is still on the stack at the RangeStmt's TRANS_LEAVE, so the name resolves to a *RangeStmt and the helper returns false whatever n.Op is. The wrapper plus its four-line comment therefore restate a case the helper decides on its own; the guard was load-bearing at the merge base, where the test was `ne.Name == "cur" && evalStaticTypeOf(...) == gRealmType` with no declaring-node check, and this diff's own helper is what killed it. Fix: delete `if n.Op != DEFINE {`, its closing brace and the DEFINE comment, dedent the loop; the live ASSIGN rejection is unaffected.
